ara2.review: Ara2 sir is very easy-going and one of the most humble faculty members. He teaches extremely well and practices many exercises in class related to each topic. He gives around 4 homework/ assignments, and quiz questions are usually taken from the homework. The midterm and final exam questions are of the same type as the practice problems. / Only the final exam includes some theory parts, such as a few MCQs and 2–3 proof-based questions. Students are required to answer only one proof question, and he informs the class in advance which proof will appear in the exam. He also gives clear suggestions about the exam pattern and often sets questions exactly as discussed. / The most important thing is to regularly practice the exercises done in class. He gives bonus marks to students who solve practice problems during class, although he does not announce it openly. He writes the names on a white paper at the end of the class. / attending all classes is essential if you do not want to miss out on bonus marks.

Theory of Computation is absolutely essential in any computer science program. I don't understand how it's not a core course. A decade or two ago, ToC would have been one of the few courses to be offered in any CS degree anywhere in the world. And nowadays it's becoming a second-class course in lieu of the more "industry-oriented" courses, which, btw, fail to be much useful in giving students the necessary skills to do well in the software industry. Sad to see CSE programs becoming substandard SWE programs. / Anywho, if you do choose to take CSE273, which you should, consider taking ARA2 sir's section. He's one of the more brilliant and true-to-the-field faculties I've come across in NSU. Also, if your goal is to secure a top grade but you're willing to be somewhat sincere about working for it, then his classes and homeworks will be more than enough to prepare you for the exams. Best of luck!
